previous_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Weston used identifiable photographs of Davies and later AI-manipulated depictions without her knowledge or consent to maintain the false Sophie persona. Possession of the source likeness was treated as permission to portray her, while the false identity induced intimate engagement and encounters with men who believed they knew Davies. The AI imagery supported these distinct identity and influence mechanisms, but the campaign began earlier; its consequences cannot all be attributed to AI use. Human selection of the tactic no longer defeats the current manipulation criteria. However, the campaign predates its undated AI phase; no identified conversation, encounter or consequential choice is matched to the synthetic portrayal. Material AI execution of the specific impaired choice therefore remains unestablished.
